title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Strategy Guide. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Three more dealt challengers (tensegrity column, shader portal, warm consumer app) wait in the re-roll pool.

options.label: The Strategy Guide
options.lineage: Printed game guides: two-spot-ink interiors, completion tables, missable warnings, 100% seals
options.thesis: The site is this month's official strategy guide: every plate a numbered exhibit, the race a completion table, the crown a printed seal.
options.viewport: Full-bleed frontispiece: the month's leading plate as the cover exhibit, vertical spine masthead at left, contents strip and dated issue line at right, the race ticket as the only spot-ink action.
options.risk: A paper world at 1am: contrast and dark screenshots must be worked hard or it reads as a flyer.

raised.raise: Ink escalates like a forging heat: the race state (open to closing to crowned) drives one spot color at total material commitment, the discipline the forge donated.

options.label: The Console Browse Screen
options.lineage: The console's own cross-media browse language: wave field, focused row, detail blooming under the icon
options.thesis: The gallery is the screen the community already stares at daily: a horizontal row of plates over an ambient field, selection blooms into detail.
options.viewport: One row of this month's plates floats mid-screen over a blurred wave field; the focused tile blooms its caption and vote ticket beneath itself.
options.risk: This is where most runs in this category land, and its shapes sit next to trademarked console UI; familiar, not fearless.

options.label: The Portrait Plate
options.lineage: Sapeur studio portrait plates: one figure, three coordinated colors, ruled caption naming every label
options.thesis: Each platinum is a studio portrait: full-length plate on a painted backdrop, a ruled caption naming every provenance under the frame.
options.viewport: One full-bleed plate centered on a flat hue backdrop, caption ruled beneath, the rest of the month's plates as a spine series at the edge.
options.case: Holds audience identification (showing off a proof like a portrait, captions per label) but loses the race clarity: a portrait series cannot carry a monthly tally or voting ritual.
options.risk: One plate per screen makes browsing slow; the series rhythm can flatten into a carousel.

options.label: The Select Rail
options.lineage: Film cutting bench: perforated rail, punched frames, grease marks, tape flags, trims on pins
options.thesis: The gallery is a strip of frames on a rail: scrub, flag where you stopped, mark states with punches and grease crosses instead of colors.
materials: one flag orange at a third of the screen
options.viewport: One rail crosses the page at a fixed height with this month's captures as frames; the flagged frame resumes where you left; spoiler marks are grease crosses, favorites hang on pins below.
options.case: Strong product clarity (screenshots are literally frames; state-as-mark fits spoiler etiquette) but the audience identification is editor-craft, not trophy-shelf pride.
options.risk: Novelty tax: every affordance is re-learned, and the rail fights long reading.

options.label: The Forge
options.lineage: Blacksmith shop: heat states, blows as rows, chalk measurements
options.case: Loses both axes fused: trophy metal as forge labor misreads a showcase, and one-blow-per-row buries the gallery.
options.kept: Total commitment to material state, whose ink-heat escalation the assigned card carries as a named raise.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark PlayStation-adjacent trophy gallery every fan site ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark hero band, monthly leaderboard card row, filter bar, grid of plates.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition is the point; you chose this branch to escape it.
